template.name: SporadicCallback
template.parameter: const int id, const int exec_time, const int length, const int releases[MAXX], callback_t type, const int BufferSize, const int amount_of_publishers, const int publisher_release_time[MAXPUB], const int publisher_id[MAXPUB], const int executorID

location.name: Waiting
location.label: y<=releases[next_release]
Waiting till the release of next callback
y <= releases[next_release]

Not at last release

In this case ("usual" case), we are waiting for poll, but also triggers release if next release-time reached.

In readyset

The callback has now been polled in ready-set (variables updated accordingly). Next the "priority" (exec_id) for the callback will be computed (in case of more callbacks of this type)

Last release

When at last release (special case), we just need to wait for polling, without the opportunity of more cb-releases.

location.name: InReadySet2
location.label: As with other callbacks, it will go to execution, when its priority is up (startExec() guard). When starting execution, the executor will sync with it, and instance recorded.
Again case for last release. Not necessary to be alert for more releases. (Repolling is not possible here, which seems wrong?!!!)

Execution without publicing

Here the callback just stays at the duration of execution, prompting the executor afterwards. There are cases for at the last release, where the callback doesn't need to be sensitive to anymore releases.

Executing with publishers

Here the callback is publishing to others, as indicated by its parameters. Again, there are cases for when this is the last release. Not much different otherwise.

transition.label: type == TIMER
poll[executorID][TIMER]?
If this is a timer and more timers polled (executor V 1), the priority has to be recalculated.
